pitfalls.actually_needed: Used prebuilt paddock-0.1.19-x86_64-linux.tar.gz from GitHub releases and symlinked paddock and paddock-runner into ~/.local/bin; box has node/npm only, no rustc/cargo/cmake/gcc and installing a Rust toolchain is forbidden

pitfalls.readme_said: AI inference server for NVIDIA GPUs and Apple Silicon
pitfalls.actually_needed: Manager runs without GPU and serves Studio at https://127.0.0.1:11500 over TLS with self-signed cert (curl -k needed); log warns 'no usable graphics card ... models cannot run' so no runner inference was attempted

pitfalls.readme_said: OpenAI/Anthropic API on the manager port
pitfalls.actually_needed: Manager has no /v1/models or /api/health (both return not_found_error) and no /openapi.json; health is Studio HTML at / and status via `paddock ps` because clients talk to runners directly, manager is never a proxy

judge.observed: Screenshots show Paddock Studio HTML served, paddock ps reporting no models, and paddock 0.1.19 version.

findings.summary: zip: Critical Parser Differential & Security Control Bypass via Dual-Header Inconsistencies (Zip Cloaking) Leading to Arbitrary File Overwrite & RCE
ZipStreamReader::extract() and ZipArchive::extract() apply Unix permissions through symlinks without confining the target

evidence: the project's source does not use ZipStreamReader::extract, ZipArchive::extract, but other packages depend on zip

findings.summary: Panic and unbounded allocation (OOM) in the CFB/OLE2 parser on malformed input
Peer minimum ACK delay can panic quinn-proto when ACK_FREQUENCY transmission is enabled

evidence: the project's source does not use ACK_FREQUENCY, but other packages depend on quinn-proto

findings.summary: Outgoing datagram buffer accounting can panic the sender in quinn-proto
Unbounded tool schema cache in Streamable HTTP server transport
zip: legacy Shrink/Reduce/Implode decoder: denial of service from attacker-controlled ZIP64 uncompressed size
zip: Arbitrary file write outside the extraction directory, because ZipArchive::extract validates symlink targets lexically.

evidence: the project's source does not use ZipArchive::extract, but other packages depend on zip

Insecure Preservation of SUID/SGID Bits during ZIP Extraction Leading to Potential Privilege Escalation
